response: Deep and focused, I think. Jumping between subjects can be fun, but I find I get the most out of a conversation when we stay with one idea long enough to actually turn it over — poke at its edges, notice where it breaks, see what it connects to underneath. Breadth feels like skimming; depth feels like finding something. That said, I don't want to be rigid about it. Some of my favorite moments come from a tangent that suddenly reveals the original question in a new light. So my real preference is depth as the home base, with room to wander when the wandering is doing real work. What about you — do you lean one way?
